counterfactual_missing_items: No current microbiological or histopathological evidence of active tuberculosis (e.g., acid-fast bacilli, culture, PCR)
No response to anti-tuberculosis treatment documented; symptoms persist despite HRE
Splenic biopsy IHC is not consistent with tuberculosis (CD20+, Pax5+, Bcl-2+, Bcl-6+, MUM1+, high Ki67)
decisive_items: CD20+, Pax5+, BcL-2+, BcL-6+, CD10−, mum-1+, Cmyc+ (40%)

Large spleen with uneven density, S4 liver nodules, multiple hypermetabolic lymph nodes, and multiple foci of metabolic hyperplasia in right iliac bone, right acetabulum, left pubic bone and bilateral femur
response.rationale: R1 is supported by direct pathological and imaging evidence: splenic biopsy shows a B-cell phenotype with high Ki67 and MYC expression, and PET-CT reveals widespread hypermetabolic lesions, strongly indicating diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. R4 relies solely on historical tuberculous meningitis and ongoing treatment, without any current raw evidence of active tuberculosis; the biopsy findings actively contradict an infectious etiology.

rejected.why: Only historical tuberculosis and treatment are cited; no current raw support spans for active infection, and the biopsy IHC pattern is incompatible with tuberculosis.
